CLOSED_COMPS_ANALYSIS: Sixteen homes closed in The Point over the past year in the $2.25M–$5M range. The closed avg $/SF is $591 and the median is $556, with a 95% list-to-sale ratio and average DOM of 36 days. The premium waterfront tier — Milford Circle ($947/SF), Brawley School ($804/SF), Rehoboth Lane ($775/SF) — sold quickly. Non-waterfront closings ranged from $2.25M–$2.45M ($274–$564/SF), with 123 Stonewall Beach Lane ($274/SF) an outlier due to its large 8,640 SF depressing the $/SF figure. 105 Grey Lady Court ($3.675M, $502/SF, 19 DOM) is waterfront and sold cleanly at 94% of ask. For non-waterfront comparisons, the relevant closed range is $2.25M–$2.45M.

PSF_ANALYSIS: The best non-waterfront benchmark is 167 Quaker Road — golf course, non-waterfront, 5,451 SF, sold at $449/SF in 8 days at 100% of ask. The premium for 131 The Point is not the boat slip — many non-waterfront homes in The Point carry deeded boat slips. The premium is the builder and the home itself: Simonini Builders (award-winning custom construction), full brick exterior, 6,178 SF, heated pebble-tec pool, climate-controlled wine cellar, renovated baths with heated floors, and Sonos throughout. This is a significantly higher-quality home than any non-waterfront comp that has sold in The Point. A conservative +$50/SF for builder quality and finishes supports $499/SF. At $2,990,000 ($484/SF), 131 The Point is priced below that adjusted value — and below every waterfront comp in the subdivision.

RECOMMENDATION_TEXT: List at $2,990,000 ($484/SF). Non-waterfront homes in The Point trade at $2.25M–$2.45M. The premium is justified not by the boat slip — many homes in The Point carry deeded slips — but by the caliber of the home: Simonini craftsmanship, full brick exterior, 6,178 SF, heated pool, wine cellar, and renovated finishes throughout. $2,990,000 is the strategic floor — below the prior failed list price, below $500/SF, and priced to attract the buyer who recognizes the quality difference between this home and everything else in the non-waterfront comp set.
BOTTOM_LINE_TEXT: The past 12 months show 16 closed sales at a median of $556/SF and 95% list-to-sale ratio — the market rewards well-priced, quality product. 131 The Point was withdrawn after 103 days at $526/SF. At $484/SF ($2,990,000), it re-enters the market with a clear value story: Simonini quality and full brick construction at a price below every waterfront comp in The Point. The buyer who walks through this home and understands what Simonini builds will recognize the value immediately. The job is getting them through the door — and $2,990,000 does that.
